sources.citation: Canadian Tire product listings 0111871p, 0112004p, 0111870p (retail titles only, checked: 2026-07-31). PDPs return HTTP 403 to automated fetch; the claims come from the discovery pass, not from a page read here.

blocks: No manual located for any of the three. The only evidence is that the retail titles claim no remote and no port. Absence of a claim is not absence of a port, which is why this is unverified rather than vendor-doc — but a data bus on a cigarette-lighter-class inverter would be unprecedented, and no driver work should be scheduled against these.

models.name: 300 W Inverter with USB Port, Power-On Indicator (CT 0111870p)

refutedOnReview: REFUTED — and refuted by the claim's own text, before any external check.  **1. The claim is self-refuting.** The dialect asserts these three models "share one register map." Its own evidence field says: "None, and that is the honest answer. These three are grouped by a shared absence of evidence — no manual found, no port claimed — not by shared evidence." A shared *absence* of a register map is not a shared registe
gotchas: 0111870p is a 300 W cigarette-lighter-class unit. Its 'USB Port' is device charging and its 'Power-On Indicator' is an LED. Neither is a comms feature.

0112004p (2000 W, CT SKU 011-2004) must not be confused with 011-2101-2, the 2000 W covered by manual 011-2102-0 in the vendor-doc dialect above. Different part numbers. Whether they are the same product is unestablished, and assuming so would launder a vendor-doc tag onto a model that has not earned it.

docs/catalog/no-comms.md already carries used-market Motomaster inverter rows (011-2106-2 1500 W, a portable digital 3000 W, an Eliminator 2000 W, 400 W, 100 W, 75 W) under 'Inverters with no comms'. These retail SKUs belong on the same page; check for duplicate rows before adding.
WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: any instruction manual, or a rear-panel photo showing only AC outlets and DC terminals.
